presentation: Always hard to define myself: I am a DevOps Engineer, Cloud Architect, Product Owner and Service Owner — and each of these roles tells a piece of my 10 years working on critical, regulated cloud infrastructures. Today I oversee hundreds of microservices that serve tens of millions of operations per day on SPID and internal IAM systems, with a scope that handles millions of users. In recent years I have consistently reduced spending on microservices and databases, and brought the release pipeline to hundreds of deployments per year. From Service Owner and later Product Owner, I became the de facto tech lead of a small team and the connecting point between engineering, business, legal and compliance. I grew up in free-software activism — that is where my DevOps-first culture and my focus on cost, security and architectural sustainability come from.

items.role: DevOps Engineer • Cloud Architect • Service Owner • Product Owner — SPID, IAM, identity ecosystem
items.description:
Product management

  • End-to-end product ownership: roadmap and backlog for a scope of ~300 microservices and cloud components (SPID, internal IAM) serving tens of millions of operations/day, balancing regulatory requirements with infrastructure scalability and efficiency.
  • Agile governance: running Scrum ceremonies (sprint planning, review) to sustain hundreds of production releases/year on critical systems, with no service disruption.
  • Stakeholder management: connecting point between engineering, business, legal and compliance; I translate regulatory constraints (SPID/eIDAS) into achievable technical requirements and roadmap priorities.

Cloud-native architecture & platform engineering

  • Infrastructure modernization: led the migration of several high-traffic critical services from legacy to cloud-native within a year, with no service disruption, improving resilience, performance and cost.
  • Identity & access management: technical reference for the evolution of the IAM ecosystem (ForgeRock LDAP), which handles millions of users on critical systems.
  • Operations: third-level incident management on systems serving tens of millions of operations/day; support to the platform engineering team on the most complex escalations.

CI/CD & automation

  • Pipelines and DevOps-first culture: I built the GitLab CI pipelines from scratch to support hundreds of releases/year, promoting automation across provisioning, compliance and monitoring.

People & mentoring

  • De facto tech lead of a ~10-person team: onboarding of new hires, ongoing mentorship on Agile processes and technical tools, definition of standards and best practices.

Tech stack:
AWS (EKS, EC2), Kubernetes, Docker, Terraform, Ansible, GitLab CI, MongoDB Atlas, ForgeRock LDAP, Prometheus, Loki, Grafana, Python, Jira, Confluence.

Cloud consultant & network administrator — Technology consulting, automation and infrastructure management.

Tech stack:
AWS, Kubernetes, Docker, Terraform, Ansible, VMware ESXi, Linux (Debian/Ubuntu/CentOS), Windows Server, Cisco/Ubiquiti networking, Python.
Java development on custom CRMs tailored to clients: introduction of referential integrity, code cleanup and development of new features.
Collaboration on client POCs: definition of a serverless deployment stack for a web application and database on Amazon Keyspaces (Cassandra as a Service).

Collaboration that ended with my hiring at Infocert. Management of Linux servers, network configuration and implementation of virtualization solutions with Proxmox. Work on migration projects and management of IT infrastructures of varying complexity.
Introduction of Docker and the DevOps methodology in the company; support for the migration toward a microservices architecture with Docker and Google Cloud Platform.

Maintainer and manager of Livenet — a solution designed by the Galileo Cooperative to manage the computer fleet of the University of Verona, several thousand workstations. Migration of storage from overlayfs to ZFS: immutable workstations, improved performance, data management and service compliance.
System administration of a fleet of ~100 PCs, servers and network serving 1,500 users; administration of Google Workspace and Moodle, IT consulting in support of teaching.
Teaching on Docker and containerization to a class of ~20 students and professionals, with a focus on the practical use of these technologies in DevOps contexts.
Collaboration with Accenture to train ~20 young talents in systems engineering: teaching Linux, Windows and networking, geared toward entering the workforce.
Teaching a class of ~20 students for the EUCIP IT Administrator certification: administration of IT systems with a focus on Linux, Windows and networking.
